intro.title: Cart Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a shopping cart feature for a React application using TypeScript. You will learn how to create and manage a global state using React Context, which allows data like cart items to be shared across multiple components without passing props manually. The main technologies involved are React's `createContext`, `useContext` hook, and TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of your cart data. By the end, you'll have a functional cart that can add items, display the total, and update quantities from anywhere in your app.
intro.usecase: Cart Context is a fundamental pattern used in e-commerce applications like Amazon, Shopify, and Etsy to manage shopping cart state across multiple components. This pattern allows users to add items from product listings, update quantities in the cart sidebar, and see real-time totals in the checkout page—all without prop drilling. Developers implement Cart Context to handle complex state interactions like applying discounts, managing inventory limits, and persisting cart data between sessions. In real applications, this context powers the entire shopping flow from product pages to checkout modals while maintaining consistent state.
